## Email  
  
![](/images/email.jpg){ width=18% style="float:right; padding:15px" }

We welcome messages about:

# Share Your User Story {#user-stories}  
  
::: {.callout-note}  
## 📣 We Want to Hear From You!  
  
We are actively collecting **user stories** (testimonials) to understand and showcase how people are using LADAL resources.  
  
**Have you**  
- Copied a code snippet for your own project?  
- Learned a new method through a LADAL tutorial?  
- Attended a LADAL workshop or webinar?  
- Used LADAL materials in your teaching?  
- Applied LADAL tools in your research?  
  
If so, **we'd be extremely grateful** if you shared your experience with us!  
  
**To submit your user story**  
Write a short paragraph describing how you have used LADAL resources and what you used them for, then send it to **[ladal@uq.edu.au](mailto:ladal@uq.edu.au)**.  
  
Your story helps us understand the real-world impact of LADAL, improve our resources, and inspire others to engage with language data science.  
:::

# Contribute to LADAL {#contribute}  
  
## Write a Tutorial  
  
Do you have expertise in a method or tool that would benefit the LADAL community? We welcome contributions from researchers and practitioners at all career stages!  
  
::: {.callout-note}  
## How to Submit a Tutorial  
  
**Step 1** Download the [LADAL tutorial skeleton (.Rmd)](https://slcladal.github.io/content/base.Rmd) — a template with the correct structure and formatting.  
  
**Step 2** Write your tutorial using the template. Include text, code, and examples following the LADAL style.  
  
**Step 3** Send your completed `.Rmd` file (along with any additional files needed to render it) to **[ladal@uq.edu.au](mailto:ladal@uq.edu.au)**.  
  
**Step 4** The LADAL team will review your submission. Once approved, your tutorial will be published as an official LADAL tutorial with full attribution.  
  
We welcome tutorials on any topic relevant to language data science, corpus linguistics, text analytics, statistics, data visualization, or related areas.  
:::  
  
## Other Ways to Contribute  
  
You don't have to write a full tutorial to make a difference! Other ways to contribute include:  
  
- 🔧 **Fix errors** — help us improve existing tutorials (see below)  
- 📣 **Share resources** — point us to useful tools, datasets, or methods  
- 🎤 **Present at a webinar** — share your research or methods with the LADAL community  
- 🌐 **Spread the word** — share LADAL with colleagues, students, and networks  
- 🤝 **Become an affiliate** — join LADAL's growing network of supporters (contact us to enquire)

# Reporting and Fixing Errors {#errors}  
  
![](/images/happycomputer.png){ width=28% style="float:right; padding:15px" }  
  
Found a mistake in a tutorial? We really appreciate you letting us know — every correction helps make LADAL better for everyone. Depending on how much time you have and how comfortable you are with GitHub, there are two ways to help.  
  
---  
  
## Option 1: Report by Email  
  
The simplest approach — just send us a message!  
  
**Contact**  
- LADAL team: [ladal@uq.edu.au](mailto:ladal@uq.edu.au)  
- Martin Schweinberger: [m.schweinberger@uq.edu.au](mailto:m.schweinberger@uq.edu.au)  
  
**Please include**  
- The name or URL of the tutorial  
- A brief description of the error  
- (Optionally) your suggested correction  
  
We will investigate and fix the issue as quickly as we can. We appreciate your patience — every report is acted on eventually!  
  
---  
  
## Option 2: Fix Directly via GitHub ⭐ Recommended  
  
The most efficient option! If you fix the error yourself via GitHub, we receive an automatic notification and can review and apply your correction quickly — no back-and-forth needed.  
  
::: {.callout-note}  
## How to Fix a Bug on GitHub  
  
**What you need** A free [GitHub account](https://github.com/) (register [here](https://github.com/join)).  
  
**Steps**  
  
1. **Find the file** — Navigate to the relevant tutorial file in the [LADAL GitHub repository](https://github.com/slcladal).  
  
2. **Edit the file** — Click the pencil ✏️ icon to edit the file directly in your browser. Make your correction.  
  
3. **Submit a pull request** — Scroll to the bottom of the page, add a short description of your change, and click **"Propose changes"**. This creates a *pull request* that the LADAL team can review.  
  
4. **We review and merge** — Once we approve your fix, it will be merged into the live tutorial — with credit to you!  
  
We are working on a step-by-step tutorial to walk you through this process. In the meantime, GitHub's own [editing guide](https://docs.github.com/en/repositories/working-with-files/managing-files/editing-files) is a helpful starting point.  
:::

# Services {#services}  
  
![](/images/consult.jpg){ width=35% style="float:right; padding:10px" }  
  
LADAL offers services to members of the School of Languages and Cultures at UQ, as well as to external partners and clients — including institutions, research teams, businesses, and individual researchers.  
  
## What We Offer  
  
**Training and Upskilling**  
- Workshops on language technology and data science  
- Bespoke training sessions for research teams or departments  
- Webinars and online learning events  
- One-on-one or small group consultations  
  
**Resources and Support**  
- Access to LADAL tutorials and tools  
- Guidance on choosing appropriate methods  
- Support for corpus construction and data management  
- Advice on reproducible research workflows  
  
::: {.callout-tip}  
## Interested in LADAL Services?  
  
To enquire about services, request a workshop, or discuss a collaboration, contact the LADAL team:  
  
📧 **[ladal@uq.edu.au](mailto:ladal@uq.edu.au)**  
  
We're happy to discuss your needs and explore how LADAL can support your work.  
:::
